lecture_context.lecture_title: Lecture 4: Adversarial Robustness and Generative Models

unit.name: GAN objectives, training problems, and code-space structure
unit.description: Derives the discriminator and generator losses, introduces non-saturating generator loss, mode collapse, alternating update schedules, and latent-code operations.
unit.summary: The discriminator loss is framed as binary cross-entropy with one term for correctly labeling real images as 1 and another for labeling generated images as 0 [ts=3817s]. The generator objective is the opposite side of the game: it tries to make the discriminator’s judgment bad, but the original minimax cost creates a cold-start issue when generated images are obviously fake [ts=3939s]. Because D(G(z)) is near 0 early in training, the saturating generator cost is flat and gives tiny gradients; the non-saturating cost is introduced to give the generator a stronger early learning signal [ts=4063s]. The instructor then describes mode collapse, where the generator fools the discriminator with a narrow subset of outputs rather than learning the full data distribution [ts=4289s]. Alternating training schedules and code-space arithmetic, such as moving from “man with glasses” minus “man” plus “woman” toward “woman with glasses,” illustrate practical GAN behavior and latent structure [ts=4339s].

key_points.text: The discriminator loss has separate cross-entropy terms for real images labeled 1 and generated images labeled 0.
The original generator minimax objective tries to fool the discriminator but can saturate when D easily detects fake images.
A non-saturating generator cost gives larger gradients when D(G(z)) is near 0 early in training.
Mode collapse occurs when G learns a narrow set of outputs that fool D without modeling the full distribution.
GAN latent codes can show vector-like structure, enabling code arithmetic that changes semantic attributes of generated images.

kp_catalog.name: GAN minimax objective
kp_catalog.description: The objective min_G max_D E_x log D(x)+E_z log(1-D(G(z))) defines the adversarial game.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: Important because gAN minimax objective formalizes how the objective min_G max_D E_x log D(x)+E_z log(1-D(G(z))) defines the adversarial game, which later units use as core machinery rather than background context.

kp_catalog.name: GAN instability diagnostics
kp_catalog.description: GAN value and loss curves are not reliable progress indicators because the game is non-stationary and jointly adversarial.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: Important because gAN instability diagnostics clarifies gAN value and loss curves are not reliable progress indicators because the game is non-stationary and jointly adversarial, sharpening later modeling, analysis, or evaluation choices.
